title: The emergency contact mechanism must bypass do-not-disturb while requiring no personal information or KYC
content:
A.1.9.1.3.2.1 lists what an emergency contact mechanism must do. Required: "enterprise grade infrastructure with correspondingly high levels of uptime"; "should not require personal information or KYC from users"; "should allow segmenting of target user groups, so that required individuals are only notified when necessary"; and "should be able to bypass silent / do not disturb mode on devices to achieve an immediate response any time of day." Recommended but not required: minimal data tracking, and open source.

The interesting engineering constraint is the pairing of the second and fourth requirements. The system must be able to force a device to ring at 4am — the most intrusive capability a notification system can have — while knowing nothing personally identifying about the person holding it. Under normal assumptions, reliable paging implies identity; the anonymity regime for ACs and the non-disclosure rule for ERG members (A.1.9.1.2.3) make that unacceptable, so the mechanism must deliver urgency without identification.

Segmentation serves a subtler purpose than efficiency. If every alert reaches everyone, responders habituate and stop reacting — alarm fatigue destroys exactly the immediacy the bypass requirement buys. Restricting notifications to those actually needed preserves the signal's meaning.

The surrounding provisions treat the mechanism as critical infrastructure rather than a tool choice. It is "selected and validated by the Protocol Security Workstream Lead" (A.1.9.1.3.2), the currently approved option is PagerDuty (A.1.9.1.3.2.2), and changing it requires the Core Facilitator to act "in consultation with the Protocol Security Workstream Lead" with the recommendation "subject to a poll through the Operational Weekly Cycle" (A.1.9.1.3.2.3). No single role can swap it out.

Fire drills test it — "the results of firedrills shall be published to maintain transparency" (A.1.9.1.3.2.4) — and A.1.6.10 makes correct use mandatory for all ADs on pain of derecognition.
description: A.1.9.1.3.2.1 sets criteria including enterprise uptime, user-group segmentation, and no KYC — resolving the conflict between paging anonymous responders and knowing who they are.
